abstract: Engineering clonal reproduction through seeds typically requires the production of unreduced (2n) clonal gametes. Unreduced clonal gametes can be engineered through the Mitosis instead of Meiosis (MiMe) system, which so far has been developed in Arabidopsis, rice, tomato and Brassica napus. However, there is no universal genetic strategy to engineer MiMe as the factors regulating the number of meiotic cell divisions show functional divergence. A potential universal factor to abolish the second meiotic cell division is THREE DIVISIONS MUTANT1 (TDM1), which promotes the termination of meiosis in Arabidopsis and maize. Here, we developed transgenic tomato plants that express a tomato TDM1 allele (SlTDM1-P19L), which is expected to encode a phosphorylation-defective SlTDM1. We observed that SlTDM1-P19L lines produced a mixture of haploid and diploid gametes, which gave rise to up to 28% tetraploid selfing offspring from diploid parents with only mild effects on male fertility. In one line, the SlTDM1-P19L transgene led to co-suppression of the endogenous SlTDM1 gene, resulting in the production of hyper-reduced polyads rather than unreduced dyads or reduced tetrads, mimicking tdm1 null mutants. Together, our results show that the function of TDM1 is conserved in tomato, SlTDM1-P19L can be effective in producing unreduced gametes, and it is a promising factor to apply in MiMe system engineering.
